subject: Post-demo: Stratus inference comparison — microburst & sustained throughput next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratus.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Stratus inference comparison — microburst & sustained throughput next steps

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great questions from your infra and ML teams. This thread is a quick written recap and a concrete set of next tests so everyone (internal + Stratus) can align.

Recap (high-level):
- Primary ask: quantify end-to-end tail latency under production-like microbursts and steady-state tokens/sec for your LLM endpoint.
- Comparison target: your current hyperscaler-managed endpoint vs Redwood Dedicated/Hosted running a matched model family.

Proposed verification plan (two A/B test vectors):
1) Microburst (short, high-concurrency spikes): 50 concurrent streams for 30s bursts; sequence length mix: 8/32/128 tokens (70/20/10%); measure p95/p99, cold vs hot KV cache.
2) Sustained throughput (steady long-run): 1k tokens/sec sustained for 20 minutes; capture tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and median/p95 latency.

Configs we suggest to keep results comparable:
- Model family: 1.3B-class evaluation (int8 on Redwood vs fp16 on hyperscaler)
- Input distribution: sample set (we'll provide 5000 example prompts)
- Warmup: 200 warmup requests; KV cache warmup for microburst test
- Batching window: 20ms continuous batching (configurable)

Deliverables from Redwood:
- bench-config.yaml (attached) with exact driver params
- microburst-load-profile.json (attached)
- p95-p99-sample-logs.txt with example log lines we will collect

Questions for Stratus:
- Can you share a small representative prompt set (500–1000 prompts) or point us to an S3 bucket?
- Are you OK with us running Redwood-hosted tests from us-west-2? If you prefer eu-west-1 we can mirror.
- Any constraints on TLS/cert pinning or IP allow-listing for load generators?

Proposed timeline: 1) confirm payload and infra by EOD Wednesday (7/31), 2) test window early next week, 3) deliver initial report within 48h of tests.

If that looks good I'll schedule the runs and loop in infra ops.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0198

Attachments: bench-config.yaml, microburst-load-profile.json

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stratus inference comparison — microburst & sustained throughput next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear plan. Sounds like what we need. Quick answers:

- Prompt set: we'll share a sanitized S3 bucket with 750 samples by tomorrow morning (s3://stratus-temp/bench/prompts).
- Region: would prefer us-east-1 for parity with our production traffic; can Redwood run tests from us-east-1?
- IP allow-listing: yes, we need your load generator IPs (or range) so our infra team can allow them.
- Procurement: attaching a placeholder PO template; procurement will review credits/terms.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Please include a driver option to simulate cold-starts (e.g., node restarts) — we've seen tail spikes there.
- We want p99 for both token-generation latency and end-to-end request (including network).

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of Platform Engineering, Stratus.ai

Attachments: stratus-procurement-placeholder.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratus.ai>, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2028-07-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stratus inference comparison — microburst & sustained throughput next steps

Looping in a few implementation notes so we're aligned before scheduling:

- Cold-start simulation: we'll add an option to force worker process recycle between bursts (config flag: --force-worker-restart). We'll run both with and without to capture delta.
- KV / prefix cache: for microburst tests we'll do a 30s steady warmup to populate KV caches before burst windows. Important to report both "cold-burst" and "hot-burst" p99.
- Measurement: capture token-level timing (generation start/end), model-side queue wait, and total request wall clock. We'll provide example log lines in p95-p99-sample-logs.txt.
- Acceptance criteria (Stratus requested): target p99 <= 400ms for hot bursts, p95 <= 200ms sustained. We'll record whether Redwood meets those at parity settings.

Operational notes:
- Batching window = 20ms; max batch size = 64 for the 1.3B profile.
- We'll instrument GPU util + PCIe counters and include them in the report.

I'll update the bench-config.yaml to include the worker-restart toggle and push a short runbook to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-example-drive-link).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: p95-p99-sample-logs.txt

If all that looks right I'll lock the calendar invites.

—Jordan

Focus on microburst (tail latency) and sustained throughput, with both cold and hot cache scenarios.
